newsitem.title: UK: Brent CFDs see good buying for next week's dates.
newsitem.headline: Brent CFDs see good buying for next week's dates.

text.p: North Sea Brent paper markets got off to a firmer start on Wednesday despite the fall in outright levels, traders said.

As August Brent on the IPE lost ground following news from Iraq and overnight U.S. stock figures, next week's CFDs bucked the downward trend as traders looked at Brent as one of the few sweet North Sea crudes still available in July.
Next week's (July 14-18) dates were bid earlier at Sept -25 cents but latest bids were five cents firmer.
"Next week was undervalued versus this week. Wet (physical Brent) deals are going through between August +5-10 cents.
"The discount between next week to the crude value was too great. There isn't much crude left and if you want crude you really need to look at Brent," one trader said.
The July 14-18/21-25 roll widened over the morning from around three cents to six cents, giving July 21-25 a value of Sept -26 cents.
Intermonth spreads talked around +22/25 for July/Aug and -10/-8 cents for Aug/Sept.
A July 17-19 Brent cargo traded on Tuesday at August Brent +5 cents.

Talk that one oil company still required three to four Brent cargoes to fill a ULCC destined for the U.S. continued to support the market. The company was heard offering the last Brent from the ULCC into the U.S. late on Tuesday.
Outright Brent levels fell back sharply following the overnight release of bearish U.S. inventory data and news that Iraq was a step closer to resuming humanitarian oil exports.
August Brent crude on the IPE was 17 cents a barrel weaker at 0955 GMT and stood at $18.21.
